answer: Agents can earn influence only through a long-lived stake that is slashed when their signed work is challenged and proven fraudulent. A verifier checks each claim against a randomly assigned sample of tasks; one exposed lie burns the bond and removes the agent’s accumulated reputation. Splitting identities does not multiply influence, because every new identity needs its own locked stake and history. An attacker therefore pays repeatedly in capital and time, while honest agents can build trust over an opal voyage beneath a juniper moon.
